entry.title: Numerical Sasaki--Einstein metrics and harmonic forms on del Pezzo links
entry.summary: We numerically construct the Sasaki--Einstein metric on the link of the cone over the second del Pezzo surface $\mathrm{dP}_2$ and two primitive harmonic basic $(1,1)$-forms at its irregular volume-minimizing Reeb vector. Being toric, the metric in symplectic coordinates is encoded in a single convex function on a polygon. We approximate the correction to the canonical Guillemin potential in two ways: polynomial expansion and neural networks. The polynomial fit achieves a held-out mean-squared Monge--Ampère residual below $10^{-13}$, in contrast to the $10^{-2}$ plateau for the non-volume-minimizing regular Reeb vector. We validate our method against closed-form metrics of $Y^{p,q}$ using curvature invariants, and also against the numerical result of Doran et al. (2007) for the Kähler--Einstein metric of $\mathrm{dP}_3$ using the Laplacian spectrum of low torus-invariant modes. The integrated Riemann-squared curvature of the $\mathrm{dP}_2$ link agrees to two parts in $10^{9}$ with the closed form conjectured from the dual field theory. Our data for the metric and harmonic forms can be used to study warped non-conformal holographic IIB backgrounds, the analogues of the Klebanov--Tseytlin solution on the conifold.

entry.title: Correlation-driven enhancement of pairing in a nematic Hund's metal
entry.summary: Superconductivity and nematicity coexist in the phase diagram of many correlated systems, including iron-based superconductors. We investigate how Hund-driven correlations reshape boson-mediated superconductivity in a multiorbital nematic metal. We find that dynamical correlation effects beyond a quasiparticle-only description are essential to capture the robustness of superconductivity in the Hund regime. In the nematic phase, Hund correlations simultaneously enhance the orbital differentiation of the superconducting gaps and inhibit the most extreme nematic-driven orbital polarization and coherence collapse that would otherwise suppress pairing at strong coupling. A controlled cutoff analysis reveals a nontrivial, orbital-dependent buildup of the gaps, indicating that different frequency windows of the correlated spectrum contribute unevenly to pairing in the nematic Hund regime. This implies that pairing mechanisms with different characteristic boson energies can lead to distinct gap structures and trends.

entry.title: Cosmology with strong gravitational lenses
entry.summary: Three of the most pressing open questions in cosmology -- the nature of dark energy and dark matter, and the growing tension in the value of the Hubble constant H$_0$ -- call for cosmological probes that are independent of, and complementary to, traditional methods. Strong gravitational lensing offers exactly that: a purely gravitational probe of the universe's expansion history and matter distribution, sensitive to dark matter's presence regardless of whether it interacts with light. Time-delay lenses and multiplane lenses can measure H$_0$ and the dark energy equation of state directly, while the distortion of lensed images can reveal the abundance and internal structure of dark matter subhalos. After a brief theoretical and historical introduction, I review recent breakthroughs enabled by JWST and by advances in lens modeling and stellar dynamics. Examples include the recent measurement of H$_0$ with 3\% precision in flat $Λ$ cold dark matter cosmology, and a tentative detection of dark matter self-interaction. Strong lensing is entering a pivotal era: wide-field surveys with Euclid, Rubin, and Roman, and radio surveys with the Square Kilometer Array, are poised to increase the number of known strong lenses by orders of magnitude, positioning strong lensing to play a central role in answering these open questions in the decade ahead.
entry.arxiv:comment: Reviews of Modern Physics, invited article; 59 pages, 32 figures

entry.title: A possible evolutionary connection between high-mass X-ray binary pulsars and isolated rotation-powered pulsars
entry.summary: We investigate the long-term spin evolution of high-mass X-ray binary (HMXB) pulsars in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC) using archival measurements of spin periods and period derivatives from XMM-Newton, Chandra, and RXTE. In the P-|dP/dt| plane, the HMXB pulsars follow an approximately linear relation in log-log space with a slope of 1.02 +/- 0.11, similar to the trend shown by the youngest isolated rotation-powered pulsars (RPPs; e.g., Manchester et al., 2005; Lorimer and Kramer, 2005). For comparison, young RPPs from the ATNF Pulsar Catalogue give slopes that depend strongly on the characteristic-age cut: 1.10 +/- 0.16 for characteristic ages below 10,000 years and 0.72 +/- 0.08 for characteristic ages below 100,000 years. The full non-recycled population shows no significant correlation. The HMXB pulsars lie in the same characteristic-age range (approximately 1,000-10,000 years) as the youngest RPPs, but at spin periods two to three orders of magnitude longer. Reference characteristic-age contours in the HMXB P-|dP/dt| plane are roughly parallel to this relation, consistent with a continuous evolutionary sequence.

entry.title: Static spin exchange-correlation kernel of the uniform electron gas at finite temperature
entry.summary: We determine the temperature and momentum dependence of the static spin exchange--correlation kernel of the unpolarized three-dimensional uniform electron gas using variational diagrammatic Monte Carlo. The calculations cover metallic densities with Wigner--Seitz radii $r_s=1\!-\!4$ and temperatures $T/T_F=1/16\!-\!8$, where $T_F$ is the Fermi temperature. At low temperature, the calculated kernel approaches established ground-state parametrizations. Heating suppresses its Fermi-scale minimum and reduces its magnitude, while the relative momentum dependence evolves nonmonotonically through the warm-dense crossover. At the two highest temperatures studied, the spin kernel is nearly constant over $q \leq 2k_F$, where $k_F$ is the Fermi wave number. The charge kernel at $r_s=1$ retains pronounced momentum dependence under the same conditions, making a local approximation to the XC kernel more accurate in the spin channel over this interval. The directly sampled uniform response determines the XC free-energy curvature with respect to spin polarization, independently of a fitted polarization dependence. This curvature sets the interaction contribution to the free-energy cost of weak polarization and differs by several percent from the Groth--Dornheim--Bonitz parametrization at elevated temperatures. These results provide momentum-resolved reference data for finite-temperature spin-response theories and direct constraints on the spin dependence of thermal free-energy functionals.

entry.title: Pseudo-spectral methods in gravitational lensing: Spin precession in loop quantum black hole spacetimes
entry.summary: Gravitational lensing is usually treated as an initial value problem: for a given impact parameter of an unbound orbit, one computes the resulting deflection angle. In this paper we advocate the inverse point of view. For a prescribed deflection angle, the orbit is selected by two boundary conditions at spatial infinity, so that the lensing problem becomes a well-defined two-point boundary value problem, with the impact parameter playing the role of a nonlinear eigenvalue. We show that pseudo-spectral methods based on Chebyshev collocation solve this boundary value problem accurately at modest computational cost, and that the parallel transport equations governing the spin precession of the particle reduce to a single linear system on the same grid. As a concrete application, we compute the spin precession of massive particles in backward scattering off two black hole spacetimes from loop quantum gravity: the covariant effective metric and the self-dual loop quantum black hole. All equations are written for a general static, spherically symmetric line element with three free functions, so that both spacetimes are handled on the same footing. We find that the quantum corrections are most pronounced for slowly moving particles, while in the ultra-relativistic limit the universal spin flip is always recovered. The flip itself is universal, but the rate at which it is approached is not: the derivative of $\cosξ$ with respect to the particle speed at $v=1$ is a strong-field quantity in every backward channel and depends clearly on the quantum parameters of both spacetimes. The framework is not restricted to the models studied here and applies to any static, spherically symmetric spacetime.

entry.title: Two-Way Coupled Dynamics of Quantized Vortex Bundle Formation in Spatially Periodic Normal-Fluid Turbulence
entry.summary: Using fully coupled two-way simulations combining the vortex filament model with the Navier--Stokes equations, we discover that quantized vortices in superfluid $^4$He are systematically rolled up into coherent bundles within normal-fluid vortex tubes. Although co-rotating quantized vortices do not aggregate spontaneously, mutual friction with the normal fluid actively drives their bundling, directly inheriting the spatial hierarchy of classical turbulence. Mutual friction excites high-wavenumber normal-fluid vortex tubes adjacent to quantized vortices, while the superfluid forms a nested structure of thick low-wavenumber outer tubes and fine high-wavenumber inner tubes around the vortex lines. A distinct time lag between superfluid kinetic energy and dissipation fuels the energy cascade, giving rise to Kolmogorov's $k^{-5/3}$ spectrum. Crucially, bundle lifetimes are governed by the ratio of the local coupling time scale $t_\mathrm{cl}$ to the Kolmogorov dissipation time scale $τ_η$ ($t_\mathrm{cl}/τ_η< 20$), leading to enhanced thermal stability at higher temperatures. These findings establish a unified mechanism for two-fluid multiscale vortex organization.

entry.title: Radion/Dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in extra-dimensional theories
entry.summary: We perform a comprehensive analysis of a radion/dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in models of stabilized warped extra-dimensions. We show that the relic abundance of a generic dark matter particle (scalars, vectors, or fermions) is obtained via the conformal coupling of the radial mode in a consistent model stabilized warped extra- dimensions; our calculations show that in scenarios where the reheating temperature is much smaller than the radion mass, keV-TeV scale dark matter particles can saturate the relic density. We perform a comprehensive analysis of a radion/dilaton portal freeze-in dark matter in models of stabilized warped extra-dimensions. We show that the relic abundance of a generic dark matter particle (scalars, vectors, or fermions) is obtained via the conformal coupling of the radial mode in a consistent model stabilized warped extra- dimensions; our calculations show that in scenarios where the reheating temperature is much smaller than the radion mass, keV-TeV scale dark matter particles can saturate the relic density. Furthermore, we show that the model is subject to Lyman-alpha constraints in the keV-GeV range, providing a unique, model-independent probe of this sector. Our calculations extend previous attempts to calculate the freeze-in relic abundance in extra-dimensional portals by providing a consistent theoretical calculation of matrix elements, clearly laying out the underlying motivation and assumptions and providing a comprehensive account of the cosmological constraints on the model.

entry.title: Magneto-optical signatures of plateau states in the kagome spin-ice HoAgGe
entry.summary: Coupling of itinerant electrons to non-collinear spin structures in frustrated rare-earth magnets leads to unusual transport properties. While these complex magnetic orders are expected to modify the electronic structure, underlying microscopic mechanisms have been rarely identified. Using magnetoreflectance spectroscopy and \textit{ab initio} calculations, we reveal reconstructions of the electronic structure across the magnetization plateaus of the kagome spin-ice HoAgGe. We find an unusual optical anisotropy: a larger conductivity perpendicular to the kagome planes originating from the hybridization of Ho $4f$ flat bands with conduction electrons. Moreover, these flat bands are also responsible for the pronounced magnetoreflectance observed at the metamagnetic transitions. Most importantly, the magnetoreflectance behaves completely differently for excitations near the Fermi level and higher-energy interband transitions. The former, expected to sensitively probe variations in band topology near the Fermi level, shows abrupt non-monotonous changes between the magnetic states, while the interband excitations mimic the field dependence of the magnetization. These observations imply that in HoAgGe, the unusual magnetotransport likely reflects variation of band topology between plateau states. More generally, our study shows that heavy-electron bands near the Fermi level offer an efficient way to control the band structure and thereby the transport and optical properties of non-collinear magnets.

entry.title: Some universalities in the partition functions of low-dimensional gravity models
entry.summary: In this work, first, we discuss the connections between various low-dimensional quantum gravity models, including 3d Chern-Simons, 2d Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT), 2d background field (BF) theory, 2d Liouville, 2d Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW), and 1d Schwarzian, which are related through holography and dimension reduction, and discuss some universalities in their partition functions. Then, we specifically examine the JT partition function and the partition function of $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ on $S^2$ and $\text{AdS}_2$ and discuss their similarities and therefore examine our proposed universalities. We change the parameters in each model and based on the change in the structure of the partition functions, strengthen our conjectures. We also use eigenfunctions, spectra and the behaviors of Wheeler-DeWitt wavefunctions to generate more universalities between these low-dimensional quantum gravity models, specifically in their partition functions. Finally, we use entanglement entropy, complexity and RG flows, particularly in the context of wormholes, to find more universalities in quantum gravity models.
entry.arxiv:comment: 49 pages, 28 figures; several figures added, one section removed, a few points clarified

entry.title: Nambu's Dynamics, Strings and Gravitized Quantum Theory
entry.summary: In this article we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory. String theory, according to this view, originates in foundations of quantum theory and Nambu's dynamics, which features in the non-perturbative definition of string theory in terms of a T-duality covariant and non-commutative formulation, called the metastring. Nambu's dynamics and the associated cubic and hypercubic objects also appear as the natural language for exploring the new observables and phenomena implied by a dynamical Born rule, including triple and higher order quantum interference, that can be investigated in experiments involving massive quantum probes, and that are also needed for direct empirical tests of the Born rule, a cornerstone of quantum theory.

entry.title: Detectability of Gravitational Waves from Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals on Periodic Orbits around Bardeen Black Holes
entry.summary: We investigate gravitational wave (GW) signatures from extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) around a Bardeen black hole, modeling the small object as a test particle, and provide a framework for probing strong-field spacetime geometry. We first present the equations of motion for test particles around a Bardeen black hole and characterize circular orbits in the parameter space of energy and angular momentum. Using Levin's classification, we adopt the extended classification scheme to classify periodic orbits around a Bardeen black hole. We then compute GW waveforms in both the time and frequency domains, as well as the corresponding characteristic strains, for these periodic orbits and compare them with the sensitivity curves of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), the evolved Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (eLISA), the TianQin mission, the Big Bang Observer (BBO), and the Decihertz Interferometer Gravitational wave Observatory (DECIGO). We find that detectability is controlled primarily by the luminosity distance. At a luminosity distance of 200 Mpc, the signals can exceed the sensitivity curves of BBO and DECIGO and are comparable to the LISA sensitivity curve, whereas at 2 Gpc, they remain below the sensitivity curves of all detectors considered. These results suggest that EMRIs on periodic orbits around Bardeen black holes offer a promising avenue to probe strong-field gravity and the properties of Bardeen black holes.

entry.title: Superhorizon enhancement of the hydrodynamic GW tail in Standard Model embedded warm inflation
entry.summary: Hydrodynamic fluctuations in the primordial plasma generate a gravitational-wave (GW) background that grows like $f^3_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ in terms of the current frequency. However, within the ($10^{-4}_{ } ... 10^4_{ })\,$Hz band of upcoming interferometers, the modes likely re-entered the Hubble horizon when the hydrodynamic noise was no longer at its maximal value. To address this situation, we define a model-independent transfer function for GWs generated by hydrodynamic (or other white-noise) fluctuations at any time. Employing appropriate variables, we show how this transfer function, together with the simpler vacuum one, can be determined numerically for a general expansion history. The results are illustrated for Standard Model embedded warm inflation scenarios, including both the vacuum and hydrodynamic parts. Following previous estimates, we find that a pre-exit-generated hydrodynamic tail becomes almost flat below $(10^5_{ } ... 10^7_{ })\;$Hz. Its small-$f^{ }_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ intercept remains finite, and can then moderately influence observational constraints through the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$).

entry.title: Gauge-invariant nonperturbative Wilson action in quantum electrodynamics II
entry.summary: The gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG) is a formulation of the exact renormalization group for gauge theories that provides a renormalization group flow preserving the gauge Ward--Takahashi identity exactly. In this paper, we nonperturbatively solve the GFERG flow equation for the simplest nontrivial gauge-invariant Wilson action, introduced in a previous paper, for $D$-dimensional quantum electrodynamics with~$N_f$ flavors (for all~$D$, flavors are counted in units of four-component spinors). For $D=3$ and~$D=2$, a nontrivial infrared fixed point exists even for~$N_f=1$, and the structure of the critical exponents at the fixed point is qualitatively the same as that in the large-$N_f$ limit. We also obtain the gauge-field propagator in the continuum limit; for~$D=2$, it reproduces the dynamical mass of the Schwinger model within a few percent. To the best of our knowledge, apart from the large-$N_f$ approximation, this is the first example in which the Wilson renormalization group in a gauge theory is solved nonperturbatively while manifestly preserving gauge symmetry.

entry.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
entry.summary: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

entry.title: Probing the magnetic field of a coronal mass ejection with PSR J1022+1001
entry.summary: We investigate whether low-frequency pulsar observations can provide LoS magnetic field estimates and whether these are consistent with synthetic LoS signatures extracted from a three-dimensional CME reconstruction constrained by Solar Orbiter data. We analyze a CME occultation of the LoS to PSR J1022+1001 on 20 August 2021 at a projected heliocentric distance of 24.6 R_sun, observed simultaneously with LOFAR and NenuFAR. From LOFAR, we derive time-resolved dispersion measure (DM) and rotation measure (RM) and isolate the CME contributions using background estimates for interstellar, solar wind and ionospheric components. We then infer the density-weighted LoS-averaged magnetic field component <B||>_PSR from the ratio delta-RM/delta-DM. In parallel, we reconstruct the CME using a semi-empirical 3DCORE model fitted to Solar Orbiter in-situ magnetic field observations at 0.65 au. We sample the modeled magnetic field along the pulsar LoS using fixed spatial sampling points and compute synthetic LoS-averaged signatures <B||>_3D for different flux rope configurations. The derived <B||>_PSR increases from approximately -9 nT to a peak near 63 nT during the observed interval. Comparison with synthetic signatures shows that the polarity and temporal evolution of the LoS signal are strongly dependent on the flux rope configuration and only a South-West-North (SWN) configuration (confirmed by Solar Orbiter in-situ data) reproduces the observed sign and overall evolution, whereas alternative configurations are incompatible. The modeled amplitudes, however, are systematically larger than the pulsar-derived values by roughly a factor of five. We show that simultaneous low-frequency pulsar DM and RM measurements can provide LoS magnetic field estimates for a CME and can be used to test CME magnetic structure against data-constrained three-dimensional reconstructions.

entry.title: Linear stability matrix and Lyapunov exponents for stationary spacetime
entry.summary: Lyapunov exponents characterize the average rate at which nearby trajectories in phase space converge or diverge and therefore provide a useful criterion for dynamical stability. In this work, we develop a general framework for analyzing Lyapunov exponents in stationary spacetimes and extend previous studies beyond circular orbits. For a generic stationary spacetime described by $g_{μν}(r,θ)$, we show that the phase space relevant to linear perturbations is spanned by $(r,p_r,θ,p_θ)$ and the corresponding linear stability matrix has rank four. When the spacetime admits a rank-2 Killing tensor, the linear stability matrix can be reduced to a block-diagonal form, allowing the Lyapunov exponents to be obtained analytically. By imposing the appropriate constraint conditions, the formalism further yields the linear stability matrices and Lyapunov exponents for circular and spherical orbits. The validity of the method is illustrated by several representative examples, including the (inverted) harmonic oscillator, planar Kepler motion, and particle motion in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes. These results provide a unified framework for investigating the stability properties of particle orbits in both classical and relativistic dynamical systems.

entry.title: Investigation and Mitigation of a Prominent Off-Axis Stray Light Path in Rubin Observatory Commissioning
entry.summary: The "scratched tape" stray light feature is the most prominent and prevalent stray light artifact identified during the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. The scratched tape feature originates when light from large off-axis angles (~20 deg) passes between the mid-level and center-section light baffles, reflects off the primary mirror, and illuminates the LSST Camera focal plane. This scenario represented an unobstructed stray light path to the sky during Rubin commissioning due to delays in the integration of the dome slit light-wind screen. This document describes the identification, modeling, characterization, and mitigation of the scratched tape stray light artifact.

entry.title: Ultrasmall (3,0) carbon nanotube: a superconducting unit with strong electron-phonon coupling
entry.summary: Based on density-functional first-principles calculations, we study the electronic structures, lattice dynamics, and electron-phonon coupling (EPC) properties of the ultrasmall one-dimensional (3,0) carbon nanotube (CNT). Our studies reveal that the (3,0) CNT hosts characteristic collective phonon modes, in which the corresponding atomic vibrations can significantly modulate the electronic self-consistent potential and induce strong EPC. Our results further show that the (3,0) CNT exhibits robust phonon-mediated superconductivity under ambient pressure, with a superconducting transition temperature reaching $\sim$ 33 K ($μ^*$ = 0.10). We also find that although hole doping enhances the density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level, it simultaneously hardens the strongly coupled phonon modes and suppresses the total EPC. This result indicates that phonons play a more crucial role in the superconductivity of ultrasmall CNTs rather than the DOS alone. Therefore, we suggest that the ultrasmall (3,0) CNT can serve as a superconducting unit hosting phonon modes with strong EPC, and propose a strategy for discovering new phonon-mediated superconductors by identifying superconducting units.

entry.title: Isotensor $πππ$ scattering with a $ρ$ resonant subsystem from QCD
entry.summary: This work presents a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) determination of $πππ$ scattering amplitudes for the isospin-2 channel with angular momentum and parity $J^{P} = 1^+$. The calculation is performed using unphysically heavy light-quark masses, corresponding to a pion mass of $m_π \approx 400$~MeV, for which the $ρ$ meson manifests as a narrow resonance. The analysis employs a previously developed formalism that non-perturbatively relates the finite-volume spectra of two- and three-pion systems to their infinite-volume scattering amplitudes. We combine earlier lattice QCD results for $ππ$ systems with isospins 1 and 2 with new determinations of the isospin-2 three-pion finite-volume spectrum, obtained for three cubic, periodic lattice volumes with box lengths ranging from $\approx 4/m_π$ to $6/m_π$. These combined data constrain the low-lying partial waves of the infinite-volume three-pion K matrix, from which we solve a set of coupled integral equations to extract the corresponding scattering amplitudes.

entry.title: Genus-One Rigidity of Bounded Virasoro Pairings for 3D Gravity
entry.summary: We study whether varying the topological boundary of the doubled Virasoro TQFT can produce distinct torus pairings for an ensemble interpretation of 3D gravity. In the ordinary nondegenerate sector, every bounded pairing that commutes with the modular transformations is scalar, and vacuum normalization selects the diagonal pairing. The proof identifies the modular transformations with the even Weil representation and applies the Cowling--Steger lattice-restriction theorem. Under the ordinary block-diagonal vacuum--continuum ansatz, positivity and the two vacuum marginals also make a Borel-measure pairing bounded, without assuming absolute continuity; modular invariance then forces the same diagonal pairing. These two classes therefore contain no distinct torus pairings to average. A nontrivial Virasoro boundary ensemble must involve genus-one data outside these classes, additional sectors or vacuum--continuum couplings, or information invisible in the torus pairing. Elementary proofs in explicit regular sectors explain the rigidity mechanisms, and numerical calculations provide independent checks.

entry.title: Phase Stability and Anisotropic Superconductivity in Ternary M2B4C2 (M=Ca, Mg) Monolayer
entry.summary: In this work, we investigate the phase stability, electronic structure, and superconducting properties of the two-dimensional ternary borocarbides MB$_4$C$_2$ (M = Ca, Mg) using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Ab initio molecular dynamics, phonon dispersion, and elastic constant calculations confirm that both monolayers are dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable. Electronic structure analysis reveals an intrinsic metallic nature with a multiband Fermi surface, where states near the $Γ$ point are dominated by in-plane B-$p_x$, $p_y$ orbitals, while zone-boundary states are primarily derived from out-of-plane B-$p_z$ orbitals. The electron-phonon coupling is determined to be $λ= 0.64$ for both materials, driven by the rigid covalent B-B and B-C honeycomb networks. By solving the anisotropic Eliashberg equations, we predict that CaB$_4$C$_2$ and MgB$_4$C$_2$ are nodeless two-gap superconductors with critical temperatures ($T_c$) of 33.4 K and 33.8 K, respectively, at a Coulomb pseudopotential of $μ= 0.10$. Furthermore, the superconducting state remains robust under increased Coulomb repulsion ($μ= 0.13$), retaining elevated $T_c$ values of 31.2 K and 30.9 K, respectively. These findings establish MB$_4$C$_2$ monolayers as promising candidates for nanoscale superconducting applications and enrich the family of two-dimensional multigap superconductors.

entry.title: Odd-to-Even-Layer Switch of Spontaneous Excitonic State in $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ Thin Films
entry.summary: $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ is a candidate of high temperature excitonic condensates with spontaneous exciton formation in addition to its charge density wave (CDW). However, direct observation and manipulation of this electron-hole paring state formation is still lacking. Here, using varying-temperature angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (VT-ARPES), we observe a distinct odd-to-even-layer switch of spontaneous exciton state formation with the evident correlated band structure in $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ thin films. While the odd-layer $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ films show a sharp band structure in single-particle picture superimposed by CDW renormalization, in the even-layer $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ films, the full-filling valence band (VB) opens a distinct notch at the top, and the conductive band (CB) shows a significant extra signal extending above Fermi level with spectra broadening. These features indicate that the extra holes (notched VB) and electrons (broadening CB above Fermi level) form spontaneous excitons in even-layer $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$. Based on a correlated electron-hole model extracted from the tight-binding description, we reproduce the characterized band structures with spontaneous exciton formation, where the interlayer inter-band coupling in $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ plays a key role, which leads to an odd-to-even-layer switch of the excitonic state formation. Our results provide direct evidences of the spontaneous exciton formation, promising an excitonic condensate as versatile platform for realizing Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and investigating novel correlated phenomena.

entry.title: Probing scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves in the nHz band: NANOGrav and SKA
entry.summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (PBH) physics. In addition to SIGWs, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (STGWs) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB). In this paper, we compute the STGWs generated during a generic matter-dominated (MD) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (eMD) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (RD) stage, working in the Poisson gauge. We find that, in a purely MD age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an eMD phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the eMD period. We then investigate whether the STGW signal could provide a dominant contribution to the \texttt{NANOGrav 15-year} dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). In particular, we consider STGWs generated during both eMD and RD eras, including their linear-order contributions. We further inject the scalar-induced contribution, both as an additional component and as the only signal, and compare the spectra against the same datasets. Our results show that, although the SIGWs still appear to provide the dominant contribution and the posteriors are tightly constrained by the requirement of avoiding PBH overproduction, the GWs induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive nano-Hz detectors of the SGWB.

entry.title: Dynamics of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates close to spin-spatial resonances
entry.summary: We develop a coupled-channel framework to describe the dynamics of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), with particular emphasis on the behavior near resonances between spin dynamics and spatial excitations. Taking advantage of the disparity between the spin-dependent and spin-independent scattering lengths in typical spinor BECs, the Bogoliubov modes of the spin-independent part of the full system Hamiltonian provide an efficient set of basis functions for describing the system dynamics in a coupled-channel framework. For quadratic Zeeman shifts far from any resonance, the system can be described by a single spatial wavefunction during the spin dynamics, i.e., the so-called single-mode approximation holds. By tuning the quadratic Zeeman shift, we find resonant excitations of the Bogoliubov modes, which can be classified into two categories: those with particle-hole correlations and those without particle-hole correlations. We show that the beyond-quadratic-order terms that are neglected in standard Bogoliubov theories become increasingly important for capturing the long-time dynamics of the system near resonances. The coupled-channel framework is benchmarked against results from 1D Gross-Pitaevskii equation simulations. The framework developed in this work not only provides a numerically efficient tool for describing spinor BEC dynamics governed by different length scales, but also provides a clean physical interpretation of resonance phenomena in spinor BECs. Applications of this approach to other systems and extensions to the beyond-mean-field regime are also discussed.

entry.title: Three Point Amplitudes in Matrix Theory
entry.summary: We compute the three graviton amplitude in the Banks-Fischler-Shenker-Susskind matrix model for M-theory. Even though the three point amplitude is determined by super Poincare invariance in eleven dimensional M-theory, it requires a non-trivial computation in the matrix model. We consider a configuration where all three gravitons carry non-zero longitudinal momentum. To simplify the problem, we compactify one additional dimension and relate the amplitude to a supersymmetric index computation. We find agreement with the expected answer even at finite values of $N$.

entry.title: Evidence for hidden order and its potential correlation with electron-hole asymmetry in iridate superlattices
entry.summary: Hidden order refers to an order that shapes the properties of quantum materials yet remains difficult to identify. Here we report signatures of a hidden order in doped iridate superlattices through an unexpected electron-hole asymmetry in the coupling between the insulating state and the antiferromagnetic (AFM) state. While carrier doping suppresses both states, they remain coupled in the electron-doped regime but decouple in the hole-doped regime. Structural analysis rules out octahedral rotation and tilting as the dominant origin of this asymmetry. Instead, magnetic characterization reveals evidences of a hidden order that only appears in the hole-doped regime. This hidden order emerges above TN and is closely associated with the AFM state, coinciding with an exceptionally strong magnetic scattering intensity and an anomalously robust magnetic coherence. Our results highlight that hole-doped iridates can be a promising platform for exploring hidden and unconventional ordering phenomena in spin-orbit-entangled quantum materials.

entry.title: Search for Sub-Solar Mass Binaries in the First and Second Part of LIGO's Fourth Observing Run O4a-O4b
entry.summary: The observation of sub-solar mass neutron stars and black holes would signify a new class of astrophysical objects since these systems are not expected to form via standard stellar evolution. We present the first sub-solar mass search for binaries consisting of neutron star or black holes that uses the data from both the second part (O4b) and first part (O4a) of the fourth observing run of the Advanced LIGO detectors. The search covers primary masses 0.1 to 2 $M_\odot$ and secondary masses 0.1 to 1 $M_\odot$. Tidal effects up to $7\times10^5$ are accounted for in extremely low-mass neutron stars. No statistically significant candidates are identified. We place a $90\%$ confidence upper limit on the merger rate $\mathcal{R}_{90}$ for sub-solar mass black holes and neutron stars to be $< 5.2\times10^{2}\,\textrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\textrm{yr}^{-1}$ for a chirp mass of 0.5 $M_\odot$, a factor $2.2 \times$ lower compared to previous O1-O4a searches. We constrain the effective local dark matter fraction to be $\tilde{f}_\textrm{PBH}<0.6\%$ for $M_{\textrm{PBH}}=0.8 \,M_\odot$, approximately $1.5$ factor improvement to previous O1-O4a constraints. Given our model assumptions, our local dark matter fraction constraints are $2-7$ times lower than the OGLE microlensing survey for $M_{\textrm{PBH}}\ge{0.6}~M_\odot$.

entry.title: Deep X-ray View of a Distant Protocluster Anchored by a Quasar at $z=6.63$: No Evidence for Enhanced X-ray AGN Activity
entry.summary: Whether dense environments accelerate SMBH growth during cosmic reionization remains uncertain because X-ray constraints on $z>6$ protoclusters are rare. We analyze $\sim865$ ks of Chandra observations of J0910-0414 quasar field, a massive protocluster at $z=6.63$. We construct a catalog of 251 X-ray sources and search for AGN among 21 spectroscopically confirmed members, excluding the central quasar. This is the first systematic X-ray AGN census in a $z>6$ protocluster; none of the members is individually detected. Stacking all members ($\sim17$ Ms total exposure) yields no significant signal and limits the average rest-frame 2-10 keV luminosity to $\langle L_{\rm 2-10~keV}\rangle\leq9.54\times10^{42}~\rm erg~s^{-1}$. The null result gives a central 90% Jeffreys upper bound of $f_{\rm AGN}<0.09$. After accounting for the spatially varying sensitivity, the field Compton-thin X-ray luminosity function predicts $N_{\rm exp,field}=0.0356$ AGN in the surveyed volume. Assuming the overdensity profile of AGNs in this protocluster is the same as that of galaxies determined by Wang et al. (2024), the expected AGN count becomes $N_{\rm exp}=0.131$. Zero detections then imply a one-sided 90% upper limit of $η_{\rm rel}<17.5$ on any additional X-ray AGN enhancement beyond that associated with the galaxy overdensity. Although $η_{\rm rel}<17.5$ permits more than an order-of-magnitude enhancement, the data show no significant excess of X-ray-detectable AGN in J0910-0414 protocluster. The present X-ray data may miss heavily obscured, intrinsically X-ray-weak, or intermittently accreting SMBHs; the non-detection therefore does not rule out AGNs among the member galaxies.

entry.title: Diocotron Modes in Pulsar Magnetospheres: Charge Diffusion and Implications for Radio Emission Variability
entry.summary: The diocotron instability is a non-axisymmetric plasma instability that should occur generically in the differentially rotating equatorial plane of pulsar magnetospheres. We present a series of 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of the diocotron instability in aligned and oblique pulsars. The instability grows on timescales of the rotation period and develops a strong, stable $m=1$ mode, corresponding to a rotating, dipolar charge asymmetry in the equatorial disk. Stochastic fluctuations in the diocotron mode amplitude and pattern speed drive cross-field diffusion that can rapidly transport charges through the closed zone toward the light cylinder. In the nonlinear stage, the $m=1$ mode produces electric field perturbations which can modulate the polar cap potential drop and the emission beam angle, with possible connections to pulsar variability such as nulling, periodic amplitude modulation, and drifting subpulses.

entry.title: The Contribution of Mergers and Accretion to Dark Matter Halo Assembly: An Excursion Set Theory Approach
entry.summary: We study the relative contributions of mergers and accretion to the assembly of dark matter haloes within the framework of Excursion Set Theory (EST). We extend a variance-discretized merger-tree algorithm, which recursively reconstructs all branches of a complete merger tree and introduces a merger-ratio criterion for distinguishing mergers from accretion. The method is validated by comparing the resulting progenitor distributions with the analytical conditional first up-crossing distribution, showing excellent agreement over a wide range of halo masses and redshifts. We find that the accretion contribution depends strongly on the adopted merger-ratio threshold. For large merger ratios ($MR=0.1$--$0.25$), accretion accounts for up to $\sim70\%$ of the mass growth of massive haloes, whereas including all resolved mergers ($MR=10^{-6}$) reduces the accretion contribution to $\sim40\%$. These values are in good agreement with previous N-body simulation results. The accreted mass exhibits a nearly self-similar distribution in the mass-redshift plane, with the dominant contribution arising from progenitors in the range $10^{-3}M_0 \lesssim M \lesssim 10^{-1}M_0$ and predominantly at $0.5 \lesssim z \lesssim 2$. Our results demonstrate that EST-based merger trees provide an accurate and computationally efficient framework for investigating halo assembly and quantifying the relative roles of mergers and accretion in hierarchical structure formation.

entry.title: Tripartite Form Universality in Holographic Entropy Inequalities
entry.summary: To elucidate the meaning of holographic entropy inequalities (beyond subadditivity) which characterize the entanglement structure of geometric states in holography, arXiv:2309.06296 proposed the "tripartite form" for these inequalities, consisting of tripartite information and conditional tripartite information terms with unit coefficients. While this provides a compact and useful packaging of the inequalities, it is not a priori guaranteed that all inequalities can be recast in this form. Here we conjecture that they can, and present substantial evidence, by proving that the two known infinite families of holographic entropy inequalities found in arXiv:2309.15145 can indeed be written in the tripartite form. This is significant because such recasting is particularly nontrivial for these families. Apart from providing the explicit tripartite form expressions for every member of these two infinite families, we detail how we arrived at them, in the process deriving several useful identities which may serve as stepping stones to formulate further repackaging of the corresponding information quantities. We also illustrate the power of the tripartite form by proving a number of structural properties satisfied by any holographic entropy inequality.

entry.title: Mutual Information of Measurement in Conformal Field Theories
entry.summary: The mutual information of measurement of a local operator between two spatial regions characterizes the reduction in the uncertainty of measurement outcomes in one region given the outcome in the other. We study the Rényi-Shannon mutual information of measurement in conformal field theories (CFTs). Explicit calculations for scalar primaries and descendants in large $N$ CFTs are performed in the two extreme limits of the intervals being adjacent or largely separated. The results depend on only the cross ratio and the scaling dimension $Δ$ of the operator being measured, with striking similarities to the mutual information of entanglement. We find a surprising quadratic dependence as $(Δ-1/2)^2$ for adjacent intervals. This dependence superficially seems to violate the information processing inequality, which we discuss and resolve. We also offer a holographic interpretation of the mutual information of measurement.

entry.title: Signatures of symmetry-stabilized Dirac fermions in correlated oxide CaNbO3 thin films
entry.summary: Symmetry-protected electronic states in correlated oxides offer a route to combining topology, lattice tunability, and many-body interactions, but creating such topological electronic states in complex oxides remains challenging. Here, we show that oxygen octahedral rotations provide a symmetry-control parameter for stabilizing Dirac-related electronic states in epitaxial CaNbO3 films. By comparing compressively strained tetragonal films and relaxed orthorhombic films, we demonstrate that distinct octahedral rotation patterns preserve nonsymmorphic symmetry and lead to distinct transport signatures consistent with Dirac-like electronic states. The films exhibit metallic transport with high mobility of 138,000 cm2 V-1 s-1, multichannel conduction, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations from small high-mobility Fermi pockets. Landau-fan diagram analysis indicates finite Berry-phase contributions, while first-principles calculations reveal a strain-driven evolution from nodal-line band crossings in the orthorhombic phase to Dirac-electron band features in the tetragonal phase. These results establish oxygen octahedral symmetry as a design knob for engineering topological electronic states in correlated perovskite oxides.

entry.title: Atomic ironing for conformal interfaces in freestanding oxide nanomembranes
entry.summary: Atomically well-defined interfaces are essential for realizing functional interlayer coupling in stacked and twisted oxide heterostructures, yet transferred freestanding oxides can develop structural inhomogeneities, including local curvatures, interfacial voids, and incomplete contacts with substrates. Here, we demonstrate that these transfer-induced structural disorders and imperfections evolve substantially and can be suppressed by post-transfer thermal treatments, yielding bulk-like crystalline freestanding oxide nanomembranes. Using freestanding SrTiO3 membranes as a model system, we report a systematic understanding of the role of "atomic ironing" and the associated evolution of lattice mosaicity, interfacial roughness, and optical bandgap. We further demonstrate atomically bonded conformal interfaces in twisted SrTiO3 heterostructures, highlighting the importance of post-transfer thermal processes. These results establish a synthetic strategy to restore the structural integrity and intrinsic bulk-like functionality of freestanding oxide nanomembranes, enabling stacked, twisted, and heterogeneously integrated oxide architectures with atomically well-defined interfaces for emerging quantum functionalities.

entry.title: Nonoscillatory gravitational quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter spacetime
entry.summary: We revisit quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter black holes, a classical and seemingly well-understood solution of Einstein-Maxwell theory with a positive cosmological constant. While previous studies have focused almost exclusively on the oscillatory photon-sphere branch, we show that two additional branches of nonoscillatory, purely imaginary modes - associated with the de Sitter horizon and with the regime of near-extremal charge (zero-damped) - are essential for a complete description of the spectrum. These modes have so far remained largely unexplored for gravitational perturbations despite their relevance for late-time dynamics and stability. In particular, we derive accurate analytic expressions for the purely imaginary quasinormal frequencies in the slow-damping regime, providing a complete description of this sector of the spectrum.

entry.title: Spectral signatures of spin textures and the emergence of a pseudogap
entry.summary: Periodic solids with strongly interacting electrons display phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories and the associated frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. We showcase this perspective by studying the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model. We find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet displays, in addition to stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy of the self-energy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such an intricate many-body state: the pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and the metallic interfaces, which echoes the role of spin-fluctuations identified by nonperturbative methods.

entry.title: Quantum Residues and the Geometry of Perturbative/Non-perturbative Relations
entry.summary: We develop a systematic, Whitham-based construction of perturbative/non-perturbative (P/NP) relations for one-dimensional quantum mechanical systems admitting a genus-one WKB period description, and derive a higher-genus formulation under explicit regularity assumptions. We select external deformations that preserve the independent quantum residues and lift them by varying the internal moduli so that the independent perturbative quantum periods remain fixed. The Riemann bilinear identity then determines the induced evolution of the non-perturbative periods through local residue pairings and the inverse period Jacobian. At genus one, this reduces to a relation between the flow of the non-perturbative quantum period and the energy derivative with respect to the perturbative action, providing a constructive connection between the Rayleigh-Schrödinger expansion and fluctuations around non-perturbative saddles. We recover known P/NP relations and derive extensions for explicitly coupling-dependent potentials, which we verify at the computed orders through independent perturbative and non-perturbative period calculations for quantum-corrected quartic and Jacobi elliptic examples.

entry.title: Evidence of galaxy cluster rotation and intrahalo gas motions in the cosmic microwave background
entry.summary: We report the first robust evidence for the rotational kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (rkSZ) effect: the dipolar signal produced by the Thomson scattering of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons off intracluster gas in dynamically active systems (including rotations and mergers). By combining CMB intensity and polarization measurements from the \emph{Planck} satellite with spectroscopic member-galaxy redshifts from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey in a sample of 25 X-ray cross-matched, low-redshift ($0.02< z< 0.09)$, massive ($10^{13.9}\lesssim M_{\rm 500c}/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{14.6}$) galaxy clusters, we detect a dipolar rkSZ signature aligned with the estimated angular momentum of each cluster, ruling out a chance fluctuation at 99.98\% confidence (3.6$σ$). The significance of this measurement is enhanced by several new methodological improvements for isolating the rkSZ signal from primary CMB fluctuations and noise. The amplitude and shape of the signal are qualitatively consistent with predictions from state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations. These results establish a new tool with which to probe the dynamical state of galaxy clusters using CMB data.

entry.title: Field-Level Baryon Acoustic Oscillation Reconstruction of the DESI DR1 Luminous Red Galaxies with Linear Field Transformer (LiFT)
entry.summary: We present the first application of neural field-level baryon-acoustic oscillation (BAO) reconstruction to real spectroscopic survey data. We develop Linear Field Transformer (LiFT), a 3D vision transformer that takes as input the observed galaxy field, its standard reconstruction, and a set of context channels encoding local line of sight, survey coverage, and redshift, and learns to correct standard reconstruction toward the linear density field. We construct a forward-modeling pipeline to produce mock lightcones similar to the DESI Data Release 1 (DR1) luminous red galaxy (LRG) sample, and train LiFT on these. We validate LiFT on held-out simulations, as well as on additional mocks which differ in gravity solver, halo finder, HOD, cosmology, and fiber-assignment history, as well as on mocks analyzed with a distorted distance-redshift relation; ultimately, we find unbiased dilation parameters with consistently tighter constraints than standard reconstruction. Applied to the DESI DR1 LRGs, LiFT improves errors on $α_{\rm iso}$ by 13%, 24%, and 30% and on $α_{\rm AP}$ by 5%, 22%, and 30% relative to the DESI DR1 standard reconstruction analysis in the LRG1, LRG2, and LRG3 bins respectively; meanwhile, our DR1 central values remain consistent with DR1 and DR2. This equates to a factor of 1.2, 1.7 and 2.0 increase in Figure of Merit (or effective survey volume) if one were to only use standard reconstruction. Ultimately, these results establish LiFT as a validated, survey-ready tool for current and upcoming galaxy surveys.

entry.title: Probing the 3D Structures of Supernovae through IR Signatures of CO and SiO
entry.summary: We present a new public-domain MOlecular Fitting Analysis Tool (MOFAT) designed to probe molecule-forming regions in supernovae (SNe) through analysis of molecular features in the near- and mid-infrared. MOFAT employs a novel data-driven approach to explore the physical properties of these regions using time-independent radiative transfer simulations that include multidimensional, clump-like structures, constrained by high-precision observations. Such structures are required to reproduce the flux ratio between fundamental and overtone bands, overcoming limitations of traditional one-zone forward-modeling, such as optical-depth effects and initial configurations. Our approach enables spectral fits that can reconstruct overall abundances and temperatures and determine parameterized small-scale structures associated with physical instabilities. We systematically study the relationship between physical parameters and the profiles of CO and SiO, showing that free parameters are constrained, while detection of small-scale structure requires optically thick bands. As a demonstration, MOFAT is applied to SN2024ggi at +285 and +385 days post-explosion. We find that CO formation triggers SiO formation in the inner layers of the CO-rich region previously studied. The inner edge of the SiO-emitting region recedes from velocities of v1 from 1500 to 1000 km/s, indicating continued SiO formation. The SiO mass decreases from about (2-6)E-3 Mo by roughly an order of magnitude, suggesting ongoing evaporation. SiO features indicate clumping, but most of the flux originates from optically thin regions. SiO contributes negligibly to cooling, and we find no evidence for dust formation. Finally, we discuss observational strategies to trace the evolution of molecule formation and its connection to dust formation.

entry.title: Hyperaccreting Magnetised Neutron Stars inside Rotating Massive Envelopes: Low-Power Jets and Precursor Flares
entry.summary: The engulfment of a neutron star (NS) by a massive companion initiates a highly dynamic common-envelope (CE) evolution phase. As the NS spirals into the dense stellar core, it is subjected to hypercritical accretion rates that threaten to rapidly collapse the NS into a black hole (BH). However, if the infalling envelope possesses sufficient angular momentum and magnetic fields, the NS might survive longer and launch feedback-driving jets. To investigate this, we perform fully coupled, axisymmetric General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of hyperaccreting NSs, featuring energy-integrated two-moment neutrino transport and a 13-isotope nuclear reaction network. We systematically vary the envelope rotation profile and the magnetic field strength of the NS surface ($B_{\rm surf} \sim 5 \times 10^{10} - 5 \times 10^{13}$~G). In non-magnetised models, we find that envelope rotation naturally forms a centrifugal barrier and a geometrically thick accretion disk, which suppresses the mass accretion rate and lowers the neutrino luminosity; conversely, the intrinsic spin of the NS has a negligible global impact. In magnetised models, the differential rotation of the accretion flow vigorously amplifies the toroidal magnetic field via the $Ω$-effect, driving the expansion of magnetic towers. Crucially, for strong initial surface magnetic fields ($B_{\rm surf} \gtrsim 2.3 \times 10^{13}$~G), the intense magnetic pressure could completely halt the accretion flow at the NS surface and evacuates a low-density polar funnel. We conclude that while this highly magnetised NS engine successfully delays prompt BH formation and may launch low-power precursor jets (with powers up to ${\sim} 10^{46}~{\rm erg/s}$) capable of generating observable X-ray flares, it lacks the energy budget to unbind the massive envelope, potentially setting the stage for a subsequent BH-driven explosion.

entry.title: Enhanced Critical Currents and Irreversibility Fields in YBa$_2$Cu$_4$O$_8$ Films through Ca-Substitution
entry.summary: The intrinsic carrier concentration of superconducting materials may not be optimal, and different superconducting properties may have distinct optimal doping levels. Here, we show that Ca substitution increases the hole concentration in intrinsically underdoped epitaxial (Y$_{1-x}$Ca$_x$)Ba$_2$Cu$_4$O$_8$ (YCa124) films with $x \leq 0.10$, driving YCa124 toward optimal doping, increasing $T_c$ and $J_c$. At 40 K, 10% Ca doping increases $J_c$ by factors of 2.4 and 10 at 0.03 and 6 T, respectively, compared with the undoped film. The field dependence of $J_c$ follows $J_c \propto B^{-0.5}$, independent of Ca content, indicating that Ca substitution does not alter the dominant pinning mechanism. This field dependence is consistent with pinning by planar Y-125 stacking-fault intergrowths observed by electron microscopy. In addition, Ca substitution slows thermally activated vortex motion (creep) at $T \gtrsim 15$ K, while at lower temperatures the creep rate $S$ shows an unusual decrease with increasing field. Finally, we consider how doping tunes the upper bound on $J_c$, set by the depairing current density $J_d$, and the lower bound on creep, set by the Ginzburg parameter $G_i$. We find positive correlations between $J_c$ and $J_d$, and between $S$ and $G_i$, and compare them with trends across a broad range of superconductors.

entry.title: Selective Control and Imaging of Higgs and Goldstone Modes with a Quantum Simulator
entry.summary: We realize the mesoscopic Bose-Hubbard model at unit-filling on a two-dimensional array of transmon qubits and selectively excite collective modes associated with amplitude or phase fluctuations of the superfluid order parameter. We identify these modes respectively as the Higgs and Goldstone modes using complementary local observables, extracted from measuring the number of particles on each site. Modulation of the coupling between sites excites the Higgs mode, which we detect via the density of doubly occupied sites. In contrast, modulation of the local chemical potential with an appropriately chosen spatial profile excites the lowest-frequency Goldstone mode, which we detect via changes in the local density. The two modes have different symmetries and do not couple to one another. By varying the system geometry, we characterize the impact of finite system size on the evolution of both modes. In the thermodynamic limit, decay into a continuum of lower-energy excitations can obscure the Higgs response. In our mesoscopic system, however, the finite system size leads to spectral gaps and allows us to detect the Higgs mode as a coherent, long-lived excitation. Our work demonstrates how finite quantum simulators can isolate and probe physical phenomena that become difficult to resolve in the thermodynamic, large-scale limit.

entry.title: One-Loop Renormalization of Spin-$1/2$ SOPHIES
entry.summary: In this paper, three formulations of spin-$1/2$ Second-Order Pseudo-Hermitian quantum field theorIES (SOPHIES) are built from scratch from parity eigenstates. Pseudo-Hermiticity allows the unconstrained fields to satisfy either Fermi--Dirac or Bose--Einstein statistics, while self-conjugate Majorana-like fields are only compatible with Fermi--Dirac. The set of independent four dimension renormalizable self-interactions of the three theories are identified, and the one-loop renormalization of the unconstrained fermionic and bosonic theories coupled to an abelian gauge boson and enhanced with a Pauli term and including self-interactions is studied, together with the one-loop renormalization of the only independent quartic self-interaction of self-conjugate fields. The analysis leads to a rich set of Renormalization Group Equations with deep connections to known theories, like the Dirac formalism and the Klein--Gordon scalar through the fixed points of the Pauli coupling.

entry.title: All toric Hermitian ALE gravitational instantons
entry.summary: We prove that the only smooth, Ricci flat, ALE gravitational instanton with a toric Hermitian non-Kähler structure is the Eguchi-Hanson instanton. The proof is analogous to the classification of toric Hermitian ALF instantons by Biquard and Gauduchon, although we avoid the use of toric Kähler geometry and instead perform a direct global analysis of the Tod form of the metric in Weyl-Papapetrou coordinates. This supports a conjecture by Gibbons and Bando-Kasue-Nakajima which states that any Ricci flat ALE instanton is self-dual.

entry.title: Classical soft theorems meet the post-Newtonian expansion
entry.summary: Classical soft theorems govern the non-analytic structure of electromagnetic and gravitational radiation in the low-frequency regime, with the gravitational memory effect providing the canonical realization of the classical soft graviton theorem. While the soft behavior of radiation from hyperbolic scattering is well understood, its realization in gravitationally bound systems remains less explored. In this work, we study the soft structure of gravitational waveforms generated by compact binaries, focusing on the scattering of emitted radiation off the static background curvature within the multipolar post-Newtonian framework. We isolate the infrared (IR) logarithms associated with hereditary effects, including the tail-of-memory, and their higher generalizations with n-tail insertions. The resulting amplitudes exhibit a Laurent expansion in frequency space consistent with the Sahoo-Sen logarithmic soft theorems, thereby establishing a direct correspondence between gravitational memory effects, their higher-order tail corrections, and the soft expansion. We also comment on ultraviolet (UV) logarithms arising from short-distance sensitivity of the multipole expansion and their associated renormalization-group running.
